title: Chicken, NS as part, baked, coated, skin/coating not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide. This entry refers to a baked chicken portion that is coated, with the skin or coating not intended to be eaten because it may contain excess fat and additives.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken meat is rich in high‑quality protein that is easily digested.
Baking retains most nutrients compared with deep‑frying.
Coatings can be made from whole grains, breadcrumbs, or spices, giving a crunchy crust.
Chicken is a good source of B‑vitamins, especially niacin (B3) and pyridoxine (B6).
Various cultures serve baked chicken with different sauces and side dishes.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Protein supports tissue growth, repair, and a healthy immune system.

items.title: Low carbohydrate level
items.content: Makes it suitable for low‑carb diets and blood‑sugar control.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Help convert food into energy and support nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: phosphorus and selenium
items.content: Phosphorus is important for bone health, while selenium provides antioxidant benefits.

items.title: Low fat when skin is removed
items.content: Removing the skin reduces saturated fat, benefiting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Sodium in the coating
items.content: Prepared coatings often contain salt; choose low‑sodium options if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Trans fats in processed coatings
items.content: Some commercial breadings may contain partially hydrogenated oils, which should be limited.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the baked chicken without skin and add it to salads, sandwiches, or use as a filling for tacos. The coating can be eaten separately if it does not contain undesirable additives.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked chicken in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
